question: To which group of patients do standard precautions apply in a healthcare facility?

options.A: Patients admitted to surgical wards exclusively
options.B: Only patients diagnosed with blood-borne viruses
options.D: All patients receiving care regardless of infection status

explanation: Standard precautions are designed to be applied universally to every patient encounter to minimize transmission risks from unrecognized pathogen sources. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T3#GNS122_U2_T3_h1)

question: What is the primary assumption underlying the implementation of standard precautions?

options.A: Healthy individuals carry no risk of shedding microbial agents
options.B: All body fluids and moist tissues are potentially infectious
options.C: Infection transmission only occurs through airborne droplets
options.D: Only visible blood contains transmissible viral pathogens

explanation: Treating all moist body substances as hazardous eliminates the dangerous gamble of guessing who is infected based on outward appearance. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T3#GNS122_U2_T3_h1)

question: When is handwashing with soap and water strictly required over alcohol rub?

options.A: Following the routine measurement of a patient's blood pressure
options.B: Immediately before applying sterile surgical gloves
options.C: At the beginning of every nursing shift change
options.D: When hands are visibly soiled with dirt or body fluids

explanation: Friction from soap and water is physically necessary to remove gross organic soil and certain non-enveloped spores that alcohol rubs cannot destroy effectively. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T3#GNS122_U2_T3_h2)

question: Why must hand hygiene still be performed immediately after removing medical gloves?

options.A: Gloves can develop microscopic defects and permit pathogen passage
options.B: Hand lotion applied earlier is wiped away during glove removal
options.C: Hospital accreditation standards require a double-wash routine
options.D: Powder inside the gloves stimulates excessive bacterial growth

explanation: Tiny punctures or tears often occur during patient care tasks, allowing microbes to colonize the skin surface despite the glove barrier. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T3#GNS122_U2_T3_h2)

question: What is the correct sequence for putting on full personal protective equipment?

options.B: Gown, mask or respirator, goggles or face shield, gloves
options.C: Gloves, gown, face shield, surgical mask
options.D: Mask, gloves, protective gown, eye wear

explanation: Donning begins with the gown to cover the body, followed by respiratory protection, eye protection, and gloves pulled up over the gown cuffs last. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T3#GNS122_U2_T3_h3)

question: A nurse is preparing to irrigate a contaminated wound that is expected to splash fluid. Which combination of protective gear is most appropriate?

options.A: N95 respirator mask and sterile shoe covers only
options.B: Sterile gloves and a standard short-sleeved clinical uniform
options.C: Gloves, fluid-resistant gown, mask, and eye protection
options.D: Disposable plastic apron and clean examination gloves

explanation: Wound irrigation generates high-risk splashes, requiring full barrier coverage for hands, clothing, respiratory tract, and mucous membranes of the eyes. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T3#GNS122_U2_T3_h3)

question: What is the immediate action an individual should take after coughing into a tissue?

options.A: Wipe down surrounding chairs with an antiseptic wipe
options.B: Leave the tissue on the nearest flat surface for housekeeping
options.C: Discard the tissue and perform hand hygiene
options.D: Fold the tissue and place it inside a uniform pocket

explanation: Immediate disposal and hand cleansing prevent infectious respiratory droplets from transferring to hands and environmental surfaces. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T3#GNS122_U2_T3_h4)

question: Why is respiratory hygiene considered a source-control measure in standard precautions?

options.A: It filters ambient room air before it reaches the patient's lungs
options.B: It destroys airborne bacterial spores through chemical vaporization
options.C: It captures infectious droplets directly at the point of release
options.D: It eliminates the need for nurses to wear surgical face masks

explanation: Source control intercepts pathogens before they travel into the surrounding environment or contaminate other individuals nearby. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T3#GNS122_U2_T3_h4)

question: Which practice is strictly prohibited when handling used hollow-bore needles?

options.A: Recapping needles using a two-handed manual technique
options.B: Placing the unrecapped syringe directly into a puncture-resistant bin
options.C: Carrying the used syringe tray to the bedside treatment cart
options.D: Activating built-in safety engineered needle devices immediately

explanation: Two-handed recapping drastically elevates the risk of accidental needle-stick injuries to the fingers and hands. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T3#GNS122_U2_T3_h5)

question: At what point should a clinical sharps container be securely closed and replaced?

options.A: After every single patient injection procedure is finished
options.B: Only at the official end of each nursing shift rotation
options.C: When the outside container surface appears dusty or stained
options.D: When the contents reach the designated fill line indicator

explanation: Overfilling sharps containers crowds the opening and exposes personnel handling the waste to protruding needles. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T3#GNS122_U2_T3_h5)

question: How should soiled bed linens be handled to minimize environmental contamination?

options.A: Rolled inward and placed directly into a designated laundry bag
options.B: Folded neatly on the bedside table for reuse on the next patient
options.C: Draped over hallway chairs until housekeeping arrives to collect them
options.D: Shaken vigorously in the open ward to remove loose debris

explanation: Rolling linens inward traps organic soil and prevents pathogenic dust from scattering into the breathing zone of staff and patients. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T3#GNS122_U2_T3_h6)

question: Which surface category in a patient room requires the most frequent routine disinfection?

options.A: Ceiling tiles and upper wall ventilation grilles
options.B: The underneath framework of the patient mattress
options.C: Window glass panels facing exterior courtyards
options.D: High-touch surfaces like bed rails and call buttons

explanation: Frequent hand contact makes high-touch objects primary vehicles for transmitting hospital-acquired infections. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T3#GNS122_U2_T3_h6)

question: What is the initial emergency action a nurse must take following a contaminated needle-stick injury?

options.A: Squeeze the finger tightly to expel trapped venous blood
options.B: Apply an alcohol-based tincture directly inside the wound
options.C: Wait until the end of the shift to report the event
options.D: Wash the puncture site thoroughly with soap and water

explanation: Immediate washing reduces the viral or bacterial load entering the bloodstream through the open wound. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T3#GNS122_U2_T3_h7)

question: Which action should NOT be performed when managing an accidental skin puncture from a used needle?

options.A: Documenting the precise details of the exposure event
options.B: Aggressively squeezing or milking the wound to force out blood
options.C: Flushing the exposed skin area with clean running water
options.D: Reporting the incident promptly to the facility health officer

explanation: Squeezing or milking damages delicate local tissues and can actually increase micro-vascular absorption of infectious pathogens. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T3#GNS122_U2_T3_h7)
